correctness.rationale: For nonzero complex a,b,c, unitary diagonal conjugation removes phases. The exact upper triangular R=(I-N)^-1 has entries 1,a,ab,abc; 1,b,bc;1,c;1. Setting x=|a|²,y=|b|²,z=|c|², independently expanded Gram characteristic polynomial P_A(t)=t⁴-A t³+B t²-Ct+1 with A=4+x+y+z+xy+yz+xyz, B=6+2(x+y+z)+xy+xz+yz, C=4+x+y+z. For fixed multiset only A varies, strictly increasing with central y: exchanging central squared weights x<y changes A by z(y-x)>0. Positive tridiagonal irreducible inverse Gram matrices ensure four distinct positive roots at realizable endpoints. The equation A=H(t)=t+B/t-C/t²+1/t³ has at most three positive critical points by Descartes; the four-intersection horizontal-level interval between endpoint A values retains simple positive roots. Implicit differentiation gives d/dA Σlambda_j^q=q times third divided difference of t^(q+2), whose third derivative q(q+1)(q+2)t^(q-1)>0 for q=p/2>0. Hence all positive p power sums strictly rise; alternating P_A' signs give singular-value pattern (+,-,+,-), and operator norm grows too. I independently calculated exact Gram characteristic polynomials for rational positive triples and spot-checked p=1/2,4 moment orderings. This finite sample is not the all-real-p proof.
